newsitem.title: USA: Tengtu Intl enters Chinese joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Tengtu Intl enters Chinese joint venture.

text.p: Tengtu International Corp said Tuesday it had agreed to buy from Blue Lake Industries its 49-percent interest in a Chinese joint venture to produce educational software for the Asian country's schools.
A Tengtu official said the company would replace Seattle's Blue Lake as the partner of a Chinese company in the venture, known as Beijing Tengtu United Electronic Development Co Ltd.

He said it would issue Blue Lake two million shares and pay it $100,000 for its interest. It would also enter a new joint venture with the Chinese company, under which it would provide $12 million in working capital, he added.

The official said the company planned to raise $13.5 million through a private placement to be completed in September. The placement, to be done mostly in Asia and Europe, will offer common shares at $2.25 each with a warrant at $4 exercisable by July 30, 1997, he said.

The official said the Chinese company, Beijing Tengtu Culture & Education Electronic Development Co Ltd, had a government license to produce and distribute electronic education software for the country's elementary, junior and middle school systems.
The company, owned by Chinese state computer companies Legend Group Co, Taiji Computer Corp and Great Wall Computer Group Co, began production more than a year ago, he said.
He said the company entered into a joint venture with Blue Lake in order to get financing for the project.
